```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(Seurat)
library(future)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

#plan("cluster", workers = 5)
options(future.globals.maxSize = Inf)

data_dir <- "/omics/groups/OE0436/data/lena/output"
fig_dir <- "/omics/groups/OE0436/data/lena/output/figures/"

infile <- file.path(data_dir, "3_xenium_BroadCellTypes.RDS")
xenium_BroadCellTypes <- readRDS(infile)
```

Now we will subcluster the broad cell types that were annotated in the last step. By only analysing a subset of cells the resolution of clustering might be better since we exclude other more distant subtypes. This might improve finding for example rare T cell subtypes.

**Disclaimer**: This analysis was not finished since subtype determination was quite difficult due to missing marker genes. Later analysis (TLSanalysis) was done with broad cell types.

# CD4+ T cells

First we will subcluster the cells that were assigned to the CD4+ Tcell cluster. For this we will use the function subset and create a new object that only contains cell from one subcluster. Since the dimreductions from the previous analysis might not describe the variability of this dataset, we run them again. Its recommended to re-scale the data (https://satijalab.org/seurat/archive/v3.0/interaction_vignette.html) 

```{r}
#Subset Tcell CD4 cluster
Tcell1x <- subset(xenium_BroadCellTypes, subset = annotationRes0.3 == "Tcell_CD4")
DimHeatmap(Tcell1x, dims= 1:5, cells=500, balanced=TRUE)


#remove metadata for broad cell types
Tcell1$Xenium_snn_res.0.3 <- NULL
Tcell1$annotationRes0.3 <- NULL
Tcell1$seurat_clusters <- NULL

#re-run scaling, dimreduction and clustering
Tcell1 <- NormalizeData(Tcell1)
Tcell1 <- ScaleData(Tcell1)
Tcell1 <- RunPCA(Tcell1, npcs = 30)
ElbowPlot(Tcell1, ndims = 30) 
Tcell1 <- RunUMAP(Tcell1, dims = 1:20)
Tcell1 <- FindNeighbors(Tcell1, dims = 1:20)
Tcell1 <- FindClusters(Tcell1, resolution = 0.5)
Tcell1 <- FindClusters(Tcell1, resolution = 0.3)
plt <- DimPlot(Tcell1)+
  ggtitle("Tcell1 subcluster SCALED res 0.3")
ggsave(plt, file = paste0(fig_dir,"4_Tcell1_scaled_Dimplot_res0.3", ".png"), width = 12, height=12)

saveRDS(Tcell1, file = file.path(data_dir, "4_Tcell1.RDS"))
```

Using these markers it is not easy determining the different subtypes. Thus we can try FindAllMarkers again.

## differential gene expression analysis 

```{r}
Tcell1 <- SetIdent(Tcell1, value = "Xenium_snn_res.0.3")

Tcell1.markers <- FindAllMarkers(Tcell1, 
                                 min.pct = 0.25, #at least 25% of cell must express gene in cluster
                                 logfc.threshold = 0.25) #only genes with logfoldchange of higher than 0,25 are considered

top20_markers <- Tcell1.markers %>% 
  filter(avg_log2FC > 0) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>% 
  top_n(n = 20, wt = avg_log2FC)


# Loop through each cluster and print the gene names
for (cluster_id in unique(top20_markers$cluster)) {
  # Extract gene names as a single comma-separated string
  cluster_genes <- top20_markers %>%
    filter(cluster == cluster_id) %>%
    pull(gene) %>%
    paste(collapse = ",")

  # Print in the desired format
  cat("cluster", cluster_id, ":", cluster_genes, "\n")
}
```

We see that the number of differentially expressed genes is reduced a lot. Thus the results from the ACT tool also get less confident.

## average expression Tfh 
by calculating the average expression per cluster, it might be easier to see which clusters express the markers most.

```{r}
avg_expr <- AverageExpression(Tcell1, assays = "Xenium", features = c("PDCD1", "CXCR5", "ICOS", "CXCL13", "BCL6"))
avg_expr_df <- as.data.frame(avg_expr$Xenium)
avg_expr_df$gene <- rownames(avg_expr_df)
avg_expr_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(avg_expr_df, -gene, names_to = "cluster", values_to = "avg_expression")

ggplot(avg_expr_long, aes(x = gene, y = avg_expression, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Average Tfh Gene Expression")

#Heatmap
library(pheatmap)
avg_matrix <- avg_expr$Xenium
scaled_matrix <- t(scale(t(avg_matrix)))
pheatmap(scaled_matrix,
         cluster_rows = F,
         cluster_cols = F,
         display_numbers = TRUE,
         main = "Avg Expression Heatmap (z-scored)",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(50))

#Featureplot
FeaturePlot(Tcell1, features = c("PDCD1", "CXCR5", "ICOS", "CXCL13", "BCL6"))

```

# Bcells subcluster
```{r}
Bcell <- subset(xenium_BroadCellTypes, subset = annotationRes0.3 == "Bcell")
Bcell <- NormalizeData(Bcell)
Bcell <- ScaleData(Bcell, features = rownames(Bcell))
Bcell <- RunPCA(Bcell, npcs = 30)
ElbowPlot(Bcell, ndims = 30) # we use only 20 dims

Bcell <- RunUMAP(Bcell, dims = 1:20)
Bcell <- FindNeighbors(Bcell, dims = 1:20)
Bcell <- FindClusters(Bcell, resolution = 0.3)
plt <- DimPlot(Bcell) +
  ggtitle("Bcell subcluster SCALED res0.3")
ggsave(plt, file = paste0(fig_dir,"4_Bcell_Scaled_Dimplot", ".png"), width = 12, height=12)

saveRDS(Bcell, file = file.path(data_dir, "4_Bcell_scales.RDS"))
```
